p01.why: The initializer_list template has no members or constructor, so auto cannot deduce a list of that shape.

p02.why: tuple_size is not specialized for const Range, so the binding falls back to the private data members.

p03.why: An unscoped align_val_t: Clang accepts, GCC and EDG reject; no main.

p04.why: The program's inline placement forms return the address they get.

p05.why: The ordering classes have every member, comparison with 0, and conversion that the uses need; no main.

p06.why: A negative bound: GCC throws bad_array_new_length with no allocation call (exit 0); Clang calls operator new[] with the largest size, which throws bad_alloc (exit 3).

p07.why: The typedefs name the core types of sizeof, a pointer difference, and nullptr; no main.

p08.why: The array placement form puts each array at the buffer with no extra storage, also for a class with a destructor.

p09.why: A byte copy of a double through char and through std::byte restores the value.

p10.why: Placement new in a construct_at outside namespace std is not valid in constant evaluation.

p11.why: A call of ::operator new by name is valid in constant evaluation only inside std::allocator.

p12.why: std::allocator and std::construct_at run in constant evaluation; no main.

p13.why: construct_at replaces the Item, and the old reference gives 9; no main.

p14.why: construct_at replaces an Entry with a const member; no main.

p15.why: The nothrow form returns null, so no argument is evaluated, nothing is built, and nothing is freed.

p16.why: GCC checks the shape of every initializer_list definition and rejects; Clang and EDG drop the non-viable candidate, call take(Point), and run.

p17.why: No std::initializer_list is declared before auto deduces one.

p18.why: A std::byte array hosts the Meter, and a std::byte write reaches the int.

p19.why: construct_at makes real active, so reading whole through the old reference is rejected.

p20.why: 5 <=> Meter needs 0 <=> v on strong_ordering, which is not declared.

p21.why: Date > Date needs v > 0 on strong_ordering, which is not declared.

p22.why: The aliases name the core types; no main.

p23.why: std::initializer_list is not a class template.

p24.why: nothrow new in constant evaluation: Clang 18, Clang 22, and GCC 16 accept; GCC 14 and EDG reject.

p25.why: A scoped align_val_t with underlying std::size_t matches the library, so the aligned forms link and align.

p26.why: strong_ordering lacks the member equal that the rule requires.

p27.why: The implementation copies the static members less, equal, and greater, so the values -7, 5, and 9 come through.

p28.why: A defaulted <=> needs v == 0 (or != 0) on strong_ordering, and the class has neither.

p29.why: GCC rejects any definition of initializer_list with the wrong shape; Clang and EDG accept a parameter declaration and run.

p30.why: The int part gives strong_ordering, and nothing converts it to the declared partial_ordering.

p31.why: A braced list initializes an initializer_list<int> whose class has the wrong shape.

p32.why: 5 < Meter needs 0 < v on strong_ordering, which is not declared.

p33.why: char, unsigned char, and std::byte writes reach the int.

p34.why: tuple_size and tuple_element are specialized for Pair, and auto binds a non-const Pair; no main.

p35.why: The class template has the pointer, the count, and the constructor; no main.

p36.why: Clang gives null for each erroneous bound with the nothrow form (exit 0); GCC throws bad_array_new_length, so check returns 2 (exit 1).

p37.why: A std::byte array hosts both Readings.

p38.why: Too many initializers: GCC calls the allocation function and then throws bad_array_new_length (exit 2), Clang's call throws bad_alloc (exit 3).

p39.why: GCC throws bad_array_new_length and every handler catches (exit 0); Clang throws bad_alloc, which the first handler misses (exit 2).

p40.why: std::construct_at runs in constant evaluation and replaces the Span; no main.

p41.why: Each comparison needs only v < 0 and ==, which the classes declare; the private constructors do not matter; no main.

p42.why: A failed dynamic_cast to a reference throws bad_cast, and the program's declared classes catch it.

p43.why: new for an over-aligned type needs no declaration of align_val_t.

p44.why: No ordering class is declared before <=>.

p45.why: Converting constructors on the weaker classes serve the defaulted <=>; no main.

p46.why: Only the single-object placement form is declared, so the array placement new finds no operator new[].

p47.why: The global allocation function throws bad_alloc for a request it cannot meet, and the declared classes catch it.

p48.why: Specializations for Range and const Range serve both bindings; no main.

p49.why: align_val_t with underlying unsigned char: Clang accepts, GCC and EDG reject; no main.

p50.why: new for an over-aligned type calls the program's aligned form with the size and alignment 64.

p51.why: The declared nothrow forms link to the library, and a request too large gives null.

p52.why: align_val_t as a class: Clang accepts, GCC and EDG reject; no main.

p53.why: Only != against 0: Clang and EDG accept the defaulted <=>, GCC rejects.

p54.why: The int part gives strong_ordering, and no conversion to partial_ordering is declared.

p55.why: The new Item becomes element 1; no main.

p56.why: Elements are built out of order with std::construct_at before any is read; no main.

p57.why: align_val_t can have enumerators, and the aligned forms honor the alignment 4096.

p58.why: Size too large: GCC throws bad_array_new_length with no call (exit 0); Clang calls operator new[], which throws bad_alloc (exit 3).
